analysis:
Compared both versions of provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/Sandbox/SandboxSetupProgress.swift and examined the new SandboxSlotChange.swift, file metadata and complete supplied test patch. The confirmation helper now supports opt-in default-yes; existing calls retain default-no (head lines 459–463). EOF is also converted to an empty answer and therefore accepted with defaultYes; integration should check whether the new caller can encounter closed stdin while offering a slot-reducing change. Caller source is absent here, so this is not yet a supported security finding.
SandboxSlotChange.swift:16–30 compares add-on totals with installer plan counts, rejects unchanged/no-job plans, classifies nondecreasing counts as additions, and copies integer counts into setup options. It does not execute commands or grant serving authorization. Test changes in SandboxSetupTests.swift:593–817 describe reruns downloading/running plan mode, automatic additions, prompted reductions, skipping planning during active jobs, explicit-count behavior and installer exit-4 propagation without --force. These are mocked contracts, not proof of installer enforcement.
Relevant boundaries are TB-013/T-061/A-019 (installer execution as owner), TB-012/T-059/A-018 (VM/provider resource contention), and disk availability under T-016/T-041. Integration should examine the changed setup flow's download/execution path, plan validation, confirmation admission and preservation of the no-force/running-job contract. The supplied changes do not touch encryption, prompt/cache isolation, attestation, provider tokens or billing controls; no concrete regression in those controls is established. Only definition index summaries and selected full definitions were supplied, not the entire model detail or PR.
